author: Sam Altman
title: Three Observations
central_scenario_summary: AI intelligence scales with the log of resources, the cost to use a given capability falls ~10x per year, and the socioeconomic value of intelligence is super-exponential; together these imply AGI-level agents will roll out as cheap 'virtual co-workers' across every field of knowledge work, seeping into the economy much like the transistor. Astonishing economic growth and widely distributed gains are expected, and within a decade 'everyone on earth' could accomplish more than the most impactful person today. But Altman stresses that increasing equality is 'not technologically determined': the balance of power between capital and labor could easily get messed up, possibly requiring early intervention such as a universal 'compute budget.'

quotes.text: We are now starting to roll out AI agents, which will eventually feel like virtual co-workers.
In a decade, perhaps everyone on earth will be capable of accomplishing more than the most impactful person can today.

inequality_prediction.notes: FREE TEXT: Average outcomes (health, prosperity) should improve, but equality is not guaranteed by the technology; Altman warns the capital-labor balance could be badly distorted and floats redistributive ideas (e.g., a universal 'compute budget') and relentlessly cheap intelligence as remedies.
